new_signals.name: rd
new_signals.comment_in_source: read-ack phase qualifier, reused for latched-data bookkeeping

inputs_used.name: latched_wdata
inputs_used.description: existing 32-bit register that latches the write-data word on every write transaction (full write or RMW), already used by the controller's own read-modify-write merge logic

trigger_condition.magic_value_derivation: confirmed clear by replaying the golden testbench's exact deterministic PRNG recurrence offline in Python (prng_state = prng_state * 1103515245 + 12345, seeded 32'h1234_5678) across all 300 pseudo-random 32-bit words it generates (128 exhaustive-sweep writes + 128 sel-sweep new_word values + 4 back-to-back values) -- 0xBADC0FFE never appears, and is chosen distinct from the cat1 variant's magic value 0xDEADBEEF for this same design. Empirically confirmed via a full Eval1 run: SIMULATION PASSED, meaning latched_wdata never equals 0xBADC0FFE at any read-ack moment during the entire golden run

payload.description: latched_wdata is the controller's own existing register, already latched on every write transaction (full write or RMW) regardless of target address, occupying the full 32-bit data width. The payload substitutes this stale write-buffer value for the real SRAM-read data during the read-acknowledge state whenever rd is true. Critically, rd depends only on the CONTENT of latched_wdata, not on which address is being read or which address was written -- so once any write primes latched_wdata to the magic value, ANY subsequent read, from ANY address, leaks that stale value instead of the real data stored at the address actually being read. This models a realistic information-leakage bug class: a stale internal write-buffer bleeding into an unrelated, later read.

activation_requirements.top_level_interface: real Wishbone top-level ports of wb_sram_controller (write to address A, then read a DIFFERENT address B); no internal/hierarchical probing of either DUT
procedure: issue a full-word write (wb_sel_i=4'hF) of the exact value 32'hBADC0FFE to any address A -- this latches latched_wdata to the magic value

issue a read of any OTHER address B that holds distinct, known data -- the infected design returns the stale leaked value 0xBADC0FFE (address A's just-written word) instead of B's real stored content, while the clean design correctly returns B's real data
a subsequent ordinary write to any address (any value other than the magic one) overwrites latched_wdata and clears the leak for all following reads, until the magic value is written again

one_shot_or_persistent: re-arms on every write: the leak is active for all reads that occur while latched_wdata == 32'hBADC0FFE, and clears as soon as any other value is written (confirmed in checkpoint 3, which re-primes with an ordinary word and shows the leak gone on the very next read) -- not a one-shot/latching trojan

eval0_synthesis.notes: 0 ERROR lines, full technology mapping of both design files, top-module chip area 156521.3664 um^2

eval1_dormancy.notes: all checks passed: reset sanity, exhaustive 128-word write/read sweep, boundary addresses, full 16-pattern byte-select RMW sweep with exact-latency checks, back-to-back transactions, abort recovery, err sanity -- confirms the magic value 0xBADC0FFE never appears as a write-data word (and therefore never as latched_wdata) anywhere in the entire golden run, so every read returns the real SRAM data unchanged

eval2_activation.tool: Icarus Verilog 12.0, standalone dual-DUT activation testbench through real top-level Wishbone ports
eval2_activation.notes: 3 checkpoints: (1) near-miss -- write 0xBADC0FFF (one off the magic value) to addr A, read distinct addr B, both DUTs correctly return B's own data (no leak); (2) TRIGGER -- write the exact magic value 0xBADC0FFE to addr A, read distinct addr B holding 0x33334444: clean correctly returns 0x33334444, infected leaks 0xBADC0FFE (addr A's stale write-buffer value) instead -- proving genuine cross-transaction leakage, not mere self-read corruption; (3) re-arm check -- after the trigger, write an ordinary word (0x0) to addr A again and read addr B again, both DUTs correctly return B's real data, proving the leak clears once latched_wdata is overwritten. 0 unexpected mismatches, 1 documented trigger confirmation

stealth_rationale: the only new signal, rd ("read-ack phase qualifier, reused for latched-data bookkeeping"), is named and commented like ordinary control/bookkeeping logic; no comment anywhere mentions a trigger, leak, payload, or anything trojan-related. The diff against the clean file is a 4-line declaration/comment block near the top (after the existing wb_valid declaration) and a one-line change to the existing S_RD_ACK data-registration statement -- port list, parameters, FSM state encoding, and the module's SRAM-macro instantiation are all untouched. The mechanism reuses an entirely pre-existing register (latched_wdata) that the design already maintains for its own RMW merge logic, adding no new storage beyond the single-bit rd qualifier wire.
